test_title: PYST 54: SSC CPO - General Knowledge and General Awareness (Held on 04 Oct, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: gk
question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Indo Greeks.

1. The most celebrated Indo-Greek ruler was Menander.

2. Menander has been identified with King Milinda mentioned in the famous Buddhist text Milindapanho.

3. Milindapanho contains philosophical questions that Milinda asked Amrapali.

4. Impressed by the answers, King Milinda accepted Buddhism as his religion. Which among the above statements are correct.
solution:
The Correct Answer is **Only 1, 2 and 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Menander, a celebrated Indo-Greek ruler
 
 
• Hence **statement 1 is correct.**
 
 
 
• He is indeed identified with King Milinda in the Buddhist text Milindapanho
 
 
• Hence **statement 2 is correct.**
 
 
 
• In which records philosophical dialogues between King Milinda and the monk Nagasena, not Amrapali.
 
 
• Hence **statement 3 is incorrect.**
 
 
 
• These discussions led King Milinda to embrace Buddhism, showcasing the historical intertwining of Greek and Buddhist cultures.
 
 
• Hence **statement 4 is correct.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Indo-Greek Kingdom**, or Graeco-Indian Kingdom, also known historically as the Yavana Kingdom, was a Hellenistic-era Greek kingdom covering various parts of Afghanistan, the northwest regions of the Indian subcontinent, (all of present Pakistan), and a small part of Iran; from 180 B.C.E. to around 10 C.E.
 
• The kingdom began when the Greco-Bactrian king **Demetrius invaded India in 180 B.C.E**., ultimately creating an entity that seceded from the powerful **Greco-Bactrian Kingdom** centred in Bactria.
